title: Adolescent vaccine coverage after a school-based catch-up campaign in 41 secondary schools
abstract: Objective: to estimate coverage of the adolescent HPV, meningococcal ACWY and pertussis-containing vaccines among students in grades 7 to 9 after a spring 2026 catch-up campaign, overall and by neighbourhood deprivation. Design: a register-based follow-up of all students or a two-stage cluster coverage survey, depending on a pending data-access decision. Results will be reported when the branch that runs is complete.
introduction: Catch-up campaigns after disrupted school years restore coverage unevenly, with the smallest gains in deprived schools. District totals hide which schools and families are still missed, and registers can miss doses given outside school programs.
methods: The report will name the branch that ran and why. Both branches share the primary outcome (up to date for all three vaccines on 2026-06-30), the stratifiers (deprivation quintile and school language share) and the consent-return measures. The register branch corrects for doses given outside schools; the survey branch samples schools with probability proportional to size and checks vaccination cards.
results: No data have been collected; the design branch is not yet decided. The report will give coverage with its interval, the deprivation gradient and consent return by school and delivery route.
discussion: The discussion will set the local gradient against published gradients and state what the district will change for next year's program. It will separate what the data show about access from what they show about consent.
limitations: The stratifiers are school or area measures, not household ones. The register branch depends on a completeness correction and the survey branch on response.
conclusion: To be written once one branch has run. It will report coverage and gaps, not the effect of the campaign.
reportingChecklist: STROBE, with RECORD if the register branch runs
summary: Draft with the design branch and results left open.
